title: Ordering late-night delivery
situation: It's almost midnight and a friend texts you about ordering late-night food together.
tip: When a friend floats an idea, react first (헐/오/대박) then bounce a question back (뭐 시킬까?) — that combo is what keeps a casual chat alive instead of killing it with a flat yes/no.

turns.ko: 야 자?? 나 갑자기 야식 땡기는데ㅋㅋ
turns.en: Hey you asleep?? I'm suddenly craving late-night food lol

turns.prompt: Say you're awake and you're in — ask what to order.

choices.en: Omg me too lol what should we order?
choices.feedback: 헐 나도 reacts and matches their energy, and 뭐 시킬까? tosses it right back — perfect momentum.

choices.en: I haven't slept yet. What shall we order? (formal)
choices.feedback: Way too formal for a midnight text to a friend — drop the 습니다/까요.

choices.en: Yeah, about to sleep.
choices.feedback: Kills the chat — they're inviting you, so react and keep it going instead.

turns.ko: 치킨 vs 족발 둘 중에 골라봐

turns.prompt: Lean toward chicken and ask if they're okay with it.

choices.en: Hmm I want chicken! you in?
choices.feedback: Picks a side and checks in with 콜? — natural back-and-forth that lands the decision together.

choices.en: I prefer chicken. (formal)
choices.feedback: 선호합니다 is textbook-stiff. Friends just say 난 치킨!

choices.en: Pick one: chicken or jokbal.
choices.feedback: You just repeated their question back instead of answering it.

turns.ko: 콜ㅋㅋ 양념 반 후라이드 반 어때?
turns.en: Deal lol how about half seasoned half fried?

turns.prompt: Love it, and bring up paying.

choices.ko: 완전 좋아! 음식값은 반반 내자 ㅋㅋ
choices.en: Love it! Let's split the food cost.
choices.feedback: 완전 좋아 keeps the energy up, and 반반 내자 brings up payment clearly and naturally.

choices.ko: 반반은 진리지ㅋㅋ 근데 나 다이어트 중인데
choices.en: Half-and-half is the truth lol but I'm on a diet
choices.feedback: Funny, but it backpedals right after agreeing — mixed signal that stalls the order.

choices.en: You may do it that way. (formal)
choices.feedback: Sounds like a customer-service reply, not a friend hyped about chicken.

turns.en: ok I'll order! says it'll take 30 min

turns.prompt: Thank them and say you'll head over.

choices.en: Okay thanks! I'm heading over now lol
choices.feedback: 고마워 + 지금 갈게 wraps it up warmly and moves to action — exactly how friends close a plan.

choices.en: Thank you. I will arrive soon. (formal)
choices.feedback: Too polite — 고마워 / 갈게 is the casual register here.

choices.en: It takes a whole 30 minutes?
choices.feedback: Reads as complaining when they just did you a favor by ordering.

title: Picking a dessert at a cafe
situation: You and a friend are at a cafe staring at the dessert case, trying to decide.
tip: In person, fillers (음…, 그니까) and quick agreement tokens (그치, 그러게) buy you time and signal you're listening. Pair them with a suggestion so the decision actually moves.

turns.ko: 와 여기 디저트 다 맛있어 보여… 뭐 먹지?
turns.en: Wow everything here looks good… what should we get?

turns.prompt: Agree it all looks good and ask what they're craving.

choices.en: Right lol what are you feeling?
choices.feedback: 그러게 agrees naturally and 넌 뭐 땡겨? throws the choice back — keeps you two deciding together.

choices.en: Everything looks delicious. (formal)
choices.feedback: 보입니다 is too formal facing a friend over a cake display.

choices.en: Does all the dessert here look good?
choices.feedback: Just echoes what they said as a question — doesn't add anything.

turns.ko: 난 치즈케이크? 근데 요즘 약과 쿠키도 핫하잖아
turns.en: Cheesecake for me? but yakgwa cookies are trendy these days too

turns.prompt: Suggest splitting both so you don't have to choose.

choices.ko: 오 그럼 둘 다 시켜서 나눠 먹을까?
choices.en: Oh then should we get both and share?
choices.feedback: Solves the indecision and 나눠 먹을까? invites them in — a classic friendly cafe move.

choices.en: Yakgwa is a traditional Korean sweet. (formal)
choices.feedback: Random fact dump that ignores the actual choice you two are making.

choices.en: Do as you please. (formal)
choices.feedback: Cold and dismissive — sounds like you don't want to decide with them.

turns.en: Oh nice! what do you want to drink?

turns.prompt: Say iced americano and ask what they're getting.

choices.en: Iced americano for me! you?
choices.feedback: 아아 (iced americano) is the everyday slang, and 넌? keeps it bouncing.

choices.en: I will have an iced americano. (formal)
choices.feedback: Sounds like you're ordering from staff — with a friend it's just 난 아아!

choices.en: Coffee is bad for you.
choices.feedback: Turns a fun choice into a lecture and changes the subject.

turns.ko: 난 라떼! 자리 잡고 있어, 내가 주문할게
turns.en: Latte for me! grab us a seat, I'll order

turns.prompt: Offer to pay this round instead.

choices.en: Okay! but this round's on me lol
choices.feedback: 내가 살게 (I'll treat) is warm and natural, and it keeps the friendly give-and-take going.

choices.en: I shall take care of the payment. (formal)
choices.feedback: Reads like a waiter — friends say 내가 살게.

choices.en: Yeah, hurry back.
choices.feedback: A bit bossy and flat when they just offered to go order for you.

title: Figuring out lunch
situation: It's lunchtime and a coworker-friend asks what you both should eat.
tip: "아무거나" feels easy but it stalls the decision. The friendly skill here is to give a soft preference and a real suggestion so your friend isn't stuck choosing alone.

turns.en: It's already lunchtime lol what should we eat today?

turns.prompt: Say you're starving and ask if they have anything in mind.

choices.ko: 헐 나 완전 배고파ㅠㅠ 너 먹고 싶은 거 있어?
choices.en: Ugh I'm starving :( you got anything in mind?
choices.feedback: Reacts with energy and 먹고 싶은 거 있어? invites their idea — way better than a dead-end 아무거나.

choices.en: I am very hungry. (formal)
choices.feedback: 고픕니다 is far too formal for a lunch chat with a buddy.

choices.en: Anything's fine, don't care.
choices.feedback: Technically fine but it dumps the whole decision on them and stalls things.

turns.ko: 음… 어제 치킨 먹어서 좀 느끼한데
turns.en: Hmm… had chicken yesterday so I'm kinda sick of greasy stuff

turns.prompt: Empathize and suggest something light like kalguksu.

choices.ko: 아 그치ㅋㅋ 그럼 칼국수 같은 거 어때?
choices.en: Ah right lol then how about something like kalguksu?
choices.feedback: 그치 shows you get it, and a concrete suggestion (칼국수) moves the decision forward.

choices.en: Greasy food is harmful to your health. (formal)
choices.feedback: Lecture-y and formal — not the vibe when you're just picking lunch.

choices.en: Then let's get chicken again today!
choices.feedback: They literally just said they're sick of greasy food — wrong read.

turns.ko: 오 칼국수 좋다! 근데 거기 항상 줄 길지 않아?
turns.en: Oh kalguksu sounds good! but isn't there always a line there?

turns.prompt: Agree it gets busy and suggest going a bit early.

choices.ko: 맞아 점심엔 웨이팅 빡세지ㅋㅋ 좀 일찍 갈까?
choices.en: Yeah the wait's brutal at lunch lol wanna go a bit early?
choices.feedback: 맞아 confirms, 웨이팅 빡세다 is natural slang, and the suggestion keeps solving the problem together.

choices.en: That place is always crowded. (formal)
choices.feedback: Just restates their point in stiff 습니다 form without offering a fix.

choices.en: Then let's just skip eating lol
choices.feedback: Joke aside, it derails the plan you were both building.

turns.en: Deal! shall we head out now?

choices.en: Okay let's go let's go!
choices.feedback: 가자 is the casual 'let's go,' and doubling it adds a friendly little push of energy.

choices.en: Yes, I will depart now. (formal)
choices.feedback: 출발하겠습니다 sounds like an announcement — friends just say 가자.

choices.ko: 잠깐, 나 아직 배 안 고픈데.
choices.en: Wait, I'm not actually hungry yet.
choices.feedback: Contradicts what you said earlier and stalls the plan right at the finish line.
